assumptions: Each node is 0x30 bytes; only its +0x10 next pointer and +0x18 child-list head are read, and the +0x10 successor is loaded before the node is deleted, so the chain survives the free.
The binary inlines the loop for the first eight +0x18 levels and recurses (site 0x5d4c961) past that depth; both implement the same post-order rule, so the model states one rule.
A null head returns with no delete; a missing node, a missing field, a cycle, or a node deleted twice is not silently modelled — the model raises.

callees.contract: operator delete with (node, 0x30) for every destroyed node, in post-order

census.note: The four direct calls are the self-recursive call at 0x5d4c961, the landing-pad call at 0x5d4cb76, the teardown-loop call at 0x5d518cc, and the straight-line call at 0x5d81617; there are no tail jumps, no stored qwords, and no RELATIVE addends.

distinct_from: Open PR #2384 (visited-element teardown 0x5d516f0): that routine is this routine's caller at site 0x5d518cc, not this routine; no address overlap in the routine windows.
Open PR #2235 (recursive tree teardown 0x5f53f50): a different routine at a different address with its own caller; no address overlap.
No open PR title or code search hit for 0x5d4c8d0.

fields.rule: loaded before the node is deleted; the walk moves to it after the node and its child list are destroyed
the whole list at this pointer is destroyed, in post-order, before the node itself is deleted

not_claimed: Caller semantics beyond the four sites' argument setup and immediate surroundings; in particular what r12 denotes in the landing pad, what [rbx+0x20d0] denotes in the large function, or what the nodes denote.
Any field of a node beyond +0x10 and +0x18, and any meaning for the node contents beyond the two pointers.

routine.argument: rdi = one list head (a node pointer, or zero)

semantics: For a list head, walk the +0x10 chain in order; for each node, first destroy the whole list at its +0x18 in the same post-order, then delete the node with (node, 0x30), then move to the node's +0x10 successor. A null head deletes nothing.

sites.argument: rdi = qword at [r13+0x18], the child-list head of the eighth-level node; after the call returns, the eighth-level node itself is deleted and its +0x10 successor is processed
rdi = r12; the call sits between __cxa_begin_catch and __cxa_rethrow, so the teardown runs while an exception is being rethrown
rdi = qword at [rbx+0x18] of the current list node; after the call the caller deletes that node with (node, 0x30) and follows its +0x10 pointer
rdi = qword at [rbx+0x20d0]; the call follows a delete of the vector at [rbx+0x2108] and a call to 0x5d593f0 on rbx+0x20f0
